findings.obligation: One home for a concept the scenarios share: the queue wordings and scan-action labels decide both what the scenarios assert and what the new diagnostic reports, so the two must be the same text by construction, not by two copies that happen to agree today (nw-test-design-mandates, declare a shared concept once; and an instrument must not be able to report a state it no longer measures).
findings.observation: The new support block declares its own private copies of the owner-facing text: REPOS_READ_WORDINGS ["repos read", "repo read"] duplicates review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:63 and review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs:43, and RESUME_SCAN / SCAN_ACTIONS duplicate review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:67-73 (and the same triple in review_app_sign_in_and_ownership.rs:724). The copies are not public, so no oracle can reuse them. They agree at this commit - my run shows the printed ABSENT/PRESENT and OFFERED verdicts matching the assertions exactly - so nothing is wrong now; but if the queue's wording changes, the printer keeps reporting against the old text while each oracle reports against its own, and the EXAMINE reader is the one who pays: the printed 'the repos-read line: ABSENT' would then be a claim about a phrase the page no longer uses. Non-blocking: no assertion or falsifier depends on it, and the diagnostic already degrades loud for the one case it can detect (text present outside the status region).
findings.remediation: Give the shared owner-facing text one home: make the support's constants pub (app.rs or a small shared module beside it) and have both oracles use them instead of their local copies, so one edit moves assertion and diagnostic together. If they are better owned oracle-side, pass the wordings into show_queue_evidence rather than re-declaring them. Either way the printer must read the same text the assertions read.

observations.text: Re-review scope and commit comparison, 94514b3 (my accepted S1 record) to the reviewed clean HEAD b441715 ('git status --porcelain' empty). Relevant inputs therefore changed on both sides - the oracle's own bytes and the production it drives - so no equivalence was established and the declared command was RERUN rather than reused; I restamp nothing from the 94514b3 run. Output kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-foss-leading-openlore/505cdf38-c31c-4074-9a9b-d89ac27d7bf1/scratchpad/s1-run-b441715.txt.

The printing is allowed under 'No examiner-specific runner/value selector/verbose support mode', and I judged the rule against what the change actually is. There is no mode: show_queue_evidence runs on every execution of the suite, with no flag, environment variable, configuration key, mode parameter, feature gate, branch or second code path - nothing selects between a quiet and a verbose run, so there is no state in which the suite behaves one way for an examiner and another way for anyone else. There is no runner: the declared native command is unchanged, the test binary is the ordinary libtest one, and visibility of the output is decided solely by libtest's own standard argument (--nocapture), the same argument any reader of any test in this repository uses. There is no value selector: the helper chooses nothing the scenario drives on, returns a value both scenarios discard, and feeds no stimulus, no expectation and no assertion. The payload of the oracle is untouched - stimulus, expected and user result stay plain words with no paths or argv. The printed labels are the owner's words ('her queue', 'Resume scan', 'the repos-read line'); they carry no production symbol, no file path, no argv and no process id. What the change adds is ordinary test output that happens to be legible, which this rule does not forbid.

The semantic RED stays reachable and unmasked, judged structurally because I may not re-create it. In both scenarios every show_queue_evidence call sits strictly AFTER the then_ steps whose observation it illustrates: the first after then_the_scan_ended_interrupted and then_her_queue_offers_to_resume_and_claims_no_count, the second after then_the_scan_ended_completed, then_the_resume_read_what_was_never_saved and then_her_queue_counts_exactly. A failing assertion panics before its print is reached, so no print can run in place of a missing observation, and none can colour the failure report: the panic and its WHAT/WHY/HOW go to the failure, while the evidence goes to captured stdout. The two RED states on record are both upstream of every print - the GIVEN-stage RED I measured at 94514b3 (the config probe refusing refuse_mark_repo_read / refuse_record_account_checks, review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:89) and the business RED craft recorded with config/wiring/store landed and scan.rs untouched (both scenarios failing in then_the_scan_ended_interrupted, left "completed", right "interrupted", craft.S1.json) - so neither is altered by this delta. Capability limit, stated rather than worked around: production now implements S1, so I could not observe that business RED again in this round; re-creating it would mean editing crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs, which is read-only to me and not mine to touch. I cite craft's measurement and judge the delta's effect on it from the bytes.

What the run printed agrees, verbatim, with what the run asserted - the point of the change, and checked rather than assumed. At the interrupted moment of both scenarios: 'the status her latest run is stored with: interrupted'; status region one line, 'Your last scan was interrupted. The suggestions found so far are kept; press Resume scan to finish it.'; 'the repos-read line: ABSENT, her queue saying neither "repos read" nor "repo read" anywhere'; '"Resume scan": OFFERED'; 'the scan actions her queue offers: Resume scan' - and nothing else, so the two FRESH_SCAN_LABELS the oracle forbids there are visibly absent from the offered set as well as from the assertion. After she picks the run up, in the repo-mark scenario: 'completed', region 'Ownership re-checked: priyaraman checkmark - 1 new suggestion' then '3 repos read', 'the repos-read line: PRESENT, reading "3 repos read"', '"Resume scan": not offered', 'the scan actions her queue offers: Scan again'; the account-checks scenario prints the same two lines with '5 new suggestions'. The printed count matches the vector then_her_queue_counts_exactly asserts against the repos the resumed run read, so the diagnostic corroborates the assertion instead of competing with it. The instrument degrades loud rather than silently: the repos-read verdict is taken from the status region, and when a page says 'repos read' outside that region the printer says so in its own words instead of reporting ABSENT, and an empty region prints '(her queue renders no status line at all)'.

The added reads perturb nothing the scenarios observe. show_queue_evidence opens only '/scan/status' and '/review' - the same two public pages the asserting steps already open, through the same Browser, with no form pressed and no parameter varied - and it opens '/review' last, so it leaves her where when_she_resumes expects her (and that step re-opens '/review' itself before pressing). One of the four calls sits mid-scenario, before the store is allowed to save again and before she picks the run up, so it is the one that could in principle disturb the resume; the run refutes that: after it, the resumed run still read repos, still completed, and the queue still accounted for exactly those repos. The oracle also keeps its port treatment: the real app binary over HTTP, the real store, sign-in, ownership proof and scan, with only GitHub and the ATProto network doubled, and the count still compared against repos_read_since - the GitHub double's request log - which is independent of the store rows production counts from. Timing: the bundle states no per-test or share budget for this feature and I make no timing claim beyond the single recorded run; the four extra page reads are inside its 6.02 s for four tests, and no derogation or half-budget condition applies that would oblige a nine-run median.

Tooling and capability limits of this round. typesafe: unavailable - I ran the permitted client from a shell command with the request on stdin ('python3 scripts/jev_decide.py --request - --output -' from the installed nw-typesafe-system-one skill, two questions: the verbose-support-mode classification of this change and a grounded claim that the observations are unchanged) and it answered 'typesafe: unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY is absent from this process environment)', the same exit-3 limitation as my earlier rounds; both judgments above are therefore mine, formed from the bytes and the run. Mechanical test selection: 'code-fact impacted-tests tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs --root .' produced NO output and was killed at the 120 s timeout (exit 144) - an empty, incomplete selection, as in my earlier rounds - so selection fell back to the mechanical change set 94514b3..b441715, whose only test files are the two oracles and the one support; of those, S1 owns review_app_scan_store_failure.rs and app.rs, and I ran the declared command for exactly that suite. Also noted and deliberately left outside my judgment of the oracle: scripts/examine/review-app-oracle and .nwave/examine.json, added at bef8464 and 2188445, are the host's EXAMINE declarations, not declared S1 supports; the script locates the prebuilt libtest binary and execs it with --test-threads=1, passing no verbosity of its own, so an examiner reads this same always-on output through the standard libtest argument. Whether that host entry point is itself wanted is the root's call, not an oracle finding.

The one finding the accepted 94514b3 record left open, owned by implementation, is RESOLVED and I remove it from this record. It asked that the business RED be observed on then_the_scan_ended_interrupted after the fault seam landed but before scan.rs stopped discarding the mark_repo_read / record_account_checks errors. craft.S1.json records exactly that, in its own words: with config/wiring/store landed and scan.rs untouched, 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure' exited 101 with both scenarios failing at review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:157 in then_the_scan_ended_interrupted, left "completed", right "interrupted" - the seam reached the store and the only thing missing was the run's ending - and the same command exits 0 after the scan.rs change. The completion obligation that record carried, implementation GREEN on both scenarios, is met at this commit by my own run above (exit 0, 4 passed). Nothing in the b441715 delta bears on either fact.
